applied.quote:
First, assess the billing unit. Brex charges on a per-user, per-month schedule on Premium ($12 per user per month). For a team with 10 employees, Brex Premium costs $12 multiplied by 10 users multiplied by 12 months, which equals $1,440 per year. Brex Essentials costs $0. In comparison, Ramp offers a Free plan at $0 per user per month and a Plus tier at $15 per user per month plus an unpublished platform fee based on team size, with an advertised 20% savings on annual billing. Expensify Collect charges $5 per member per month, which equals $600 per year for 10 users ($5 multiplied by 10 multiplied by 12). BILL charges $49 per user per month on Essentials ($5,880 per year for 10 users), $65 per user per month on Team ($7,800 per year), and $89 per user per month on Corporate ($10,680 per year), while stating no per-user subscription fees for BILL Spend & Expense. Mercury and Relay charge flat monthly platform rates regardless of user headcount, with Mercury base at $0 per month and Relay Starter at $0 per month with unlimited user seats.

Second, evaluate banking and cash management structures. Brex LLC is listed as a wholly owned subsidiary of Capital One, N.A. Brex displays estimated annualized treasury returns between 3.63% and 3.98%. If your team requires a business checking account directly attached to card issuance, Mercury provides up to $5M in Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) coverage through partner banks and sweep networks, free Automated Clearing House (ACH) transfers, free domestic and United States Dollar (USD) international wires, and treasury access starting at a $250,000 balance. Ramp lists earning 2% on cash held in an FDIC-insured checking account and 4.66% in a Ramp Investment Account under variable footnoted terms. Relay offers checking accounts with tiered savings yields: 1.19% Annual Percentage Yield (APY) on Starter, 1.87% APY on Grow ($30 per month), and 3.21% APY on Scale ($120 per month shown alongside $90).

Third, examine multi-entity and accounting system requirements. Brex Essentials supports up to two business entities, while Brex Premium expands to multi-entity management across domestic and international operations. Ramp Free provides standard accounting sync with QuickBooks Online and Xero, while NetSuite and Sage Intacct integrations require Ramp Plus alongside multi-entity support. Expensify supports QuickBooks and Xero on Collect ($5 per member per month) and reserves NetSuite and Sage Intacct for Control. BILL Essentials syncs through comma-separated values (CSV) file imports and exports, requiring Team or Corporate for automatic accounting sync.
applied.replacement: Consider three structural checkpoints: - Billing unit: Brex charges per user on Premium ($12 per user per month, or $1,440 per year for 10 users; Essentials is $0). Ramp offers Free at $0 and Plus at $15 per user per month plus a team-size platform fee, Expensify Collect charges $5 per member per month ($600 per year for 10 users), and BILL charges $49 to $89 per user per month on core plans ($5,880 to $10,680 per year for 10 users) with $0 on BILL Spend & Expense, while Mercury and Relay charge flat platform fees regardless of headcount. - Banking and cash management: Mercury offers checking with sweep insurance up to $5M, free ACH and wires, and treasury at $250,000; Ramp offers a checking account earning 2% and 4.66% on investments; Relay provides checking with savings yields from 1.19% to 3.21% APY; Brex Checking is provided via Column N.A. with treasury returns between 3.63% and 3.98% for eligible tiers. - Multi-entity and accounting requirements: Brex Essentials supports two entities and Premium covers international multi-entity. Ramp Free and Expensify Collect sync with QuickBooks and Xero, requiring upgraded tiers for NetSuite and Sage Intacct, while BILL Essentials uses CSV export/import.
